# Owned downstream independent composition

Status: SOURCE ONLY. No producer has been imported or executed. The input catalog was written before these new producer sources. Root must review and approve an exact lock before first generation.

This finite extension leaves the already qualified stable/entry/event corpus unchanged. It independently composes four downstream candidate pins and identities, the original modeled owned event receipt, a signed owned seed declaration and prepared seed record, the exact card/input IDs, decoded-domain seed/result signature messages, fixed 73-byte carrier payloads, and the result v1→v2 career intent/marker/activation bytes. All field order/domains come from the adopted contract and unchanged old recipe/type snapshots. Integer Ed25519/secp256k1 arithmetic is the unchanged published Set45 Python source. Only fixture keys 1/2 and the existing named deterministic Ed25519 fixture seeds are used.

There are two deliberately different expectations. `codec_positives` contains finite values intended for their closed typed codec. `compositions` includes private marker/hash recipes and an explicitly **conditional result body**. That body retains old physical public source facts but supplies new identity bindings for byte/signature composition only. Its public old winner/method/round/tick summary is copied unchanged, not synthesized. It is not a positive full source/booking/result validator case, not a rerun of the simulation, not authenticated ownership and not a claim of actual chain finality. Tests must not feed it to a full validator and expect success. Result signature cases test the complete owned message and decoded hash bytes, rather than signing a display hex string or inherited family message. The custom SignedCheckpoint case is an encoding/fixture-signature check; its modeled target hash is not asserted to have normal PoW.

The event input is copied from the approved independent owned-consumer successor3 corpus. Its transferred-before-noon member/exclusion and immutable birth facts are not rewritten. Receipt capture fences are explicit modeled observations at noon+10ms. The original event calendar remains authoritative; the model does not substitute a fixed-week deadline. A single conditional target and one result-source shape suffice for the domain/field-order checks. It does not generate an ownership history, source completeness, C1 eligibility, new matchmaking policy or any live source capability.

`case-plan.json` fixes the finite scope. `sizing_model.py` measures only those encoded witnesses against declared caps; it does not claim a worst-case bound or total Go heap limit. Lifecycle, source authority, actual matching/simulation, finality and exactly-once career behavior remain separate concrete integration qualification.

Approved-lock schema: `approved_by: "root"`, `execution_authorized: true`, `input_catalog_sha256`, and `sources` mapping exactly the five source files to their SHA256. The root records the lock SHA externally. The entrypoint verifies exact public input inventory and all source bytes **before** importing either the model or old crypto, requires exclusive output, writes failed reports without relabeling them, and prohibits bytecode.

After approval only:

```text
python -B generate_reference.py --execute --input-root inputs --approved-producer-lock <lock> --approved-lock-sha256 <sha> --output <new-exclusive-output>
```

First Python 3.14, second Python 3.9 and a repository-only portable reproduction must produce the same `owned-downstream-v1.json` bytes. No new Go output can become an expectation.
